name: Multi-LogiEval
intro: Multi-LogiEval 评测命题逻辑、一阶逻辑与非单调逻辑的一至五步推理。论文分别组合经典逻辑与非单调逻辑规则链，用 Claude-2 生成自然语言上下文和问题，再逐条人工校验修订，形成 1,552 条论文主集；附录 H 的 70 条单步多元一阶逻辑样本单独统计，不并入主集。
org: Arizona State University, Google, Intel, UCSF
build_method: 规则组合, 自动生成, 人工校验, 混合
task_type: 二元分类, 逻辑蕴含
eval_feature: 三类逻辑, 深度 1–5, 规则组合, 人工修订, 零样本思维链, 附录扩展单独统计
scale: 论文主集 1,552 条；附录 H 另含 70 条单步样本
openness_en: Partly Public (MIT data release; no construction-generation or evaluation code)
build_method_en: Rule Composition, Automated Generation, Human Validation, Hybrid
eval_feature_en: Three Logic Types, Depths 1–5, Rule Combinations, Human Correction, Zero-shot CoT, Separate Appendix Extension
intro_en: Multi-LogiEval evaluates one-to-five-step reasoning across propositional, first-order, and non-monotonic logic. The paper separately composes classical and non-monotonic rule chains, uses Claude-2 to generate natural-language contexts and questions, and manually validates and corrects every item to form a 1,552-example paper core. Appendix H's 70 one-step n-ary FOL samples are reported separately rather than merged into that core.

drawio_review_note: Paper/source audit fixed on 2026-07-21. The primary paper is arXiv:2406.17169v3, last revised 7 October 2024; the reviewed PDF has SHA-256 8d41be5ca35b592d17cad88da974055469f712801af805b0e556ea2b78046204. PDF pages 4–7 cover Section 3.1 rule choice and chaining, Figure 2, the 71 depth-2-to-5 monotonic combinations, Section 3.1.2 and Figure 3 generation prompts, Section 3.2 non-monotonic construction, Section 3.3 validation, Table 5 statistics, and Section 4.1 evaluation. Appendices B–H on PDF pages 12–16 were also checked: B lists monotonic combinations, C gives the PL/FOL prompt, D gives natural-language examples, E details the non-monotonic patterns and prompts, F analyzes validation, G reports the separate few-shot experiment, and H defines the n-ary first-order extension. The core inventory begins from 25 rules and adds eight, yielding 33 zero- or one-variable inference rules for PL/FOL; seven n-ary FOL rules are a separate Appendix H extension. Depth one uses single rules. For multi-step classical logic, each earlier conclusion becomes part of the next rule's premise, and the paper reports 71 combinations across depths two through five. Claude-2 receives five in-context exemplars for every rule combination; those five are prompt demonstrations, not a claim that only five output items are generated. The prompt also specifies rule definitions, output format, diversity, and two tasks: produce a real-world context without symbolic entity labels and a question whose answer requires the intended chain. The non-monotonic stream starts from eight Lifschitz patterns, uses only one NM rule in a chain because each pattern already carries four or five assumptions, and manually defines 12, 2, 2, and 1 combinations for depths two, three, four, and five using NM conclusions with MP, MT, and DS. Every generated context is manually checked for the intended logical relations, story errors, grammar, and typos. The authors select or update 10 items per depth-one rule and 15 or 20 items per multi-step combination. Table 5 fixes the paper core at 1,552 items: PL 525, FOL 535, NM 492; depth counts 410, 442, 310, 280, and 110; labels 1,126 Yes and 426 No. Six models are evaluated with zero-shot chain-of-thought on prompt + context + question, predicting Yes or No, and the paper reports Accuracy by logic type and depth plus reasoning-chain analysis. Appendix H is deliberately dashed and outside the core: it reports seven n-ary FOL rules, 10 items each (70 paper samples), one-step reasoning only, and a separate three-large-model evaluation. The fixed official source is https://github.com/Mihir3009/Multi-LogiEval/tree/6d55ade5dfcc35e1382bf62335df3a061bc4c781 at main commit 6d55ade5dfcc35e1382bf62335df3a061bc4c781; its repository LICENSE is MIT. Its checked tree contains only README.md, LICENSE, and data JSON files—no construction generator, Claude-2 runner, evaluator, parser, or scoring implementation—so end-to-end construction and evaluation code remain undisclosed and the site labels the benchmark partly public. A direct parse of all fixed-tree sample arrays exposes release drift that must not be silently merged into the paper claim: the five d1–d5 directories contain 1,556 JSON sample entries rather than the paper's 1,552 (d2 totals 446 rather than 442), while multivariable_fol_Data contains 140 entries rather than Appendix H's stated 70; the whole tree totals 1,696 entries across 111 JSON files. The diagram therefore labels 1,552 and 70 as paper quantities and puts the fixed Git counts in a dashed published-surface node. The canonical English and Chinese specs use identical positions and topology; solid connectors encode the core causal path, while Appendix H and publication evidence are explicit dashed secondary branches. This is a source-only audit: formal Draw.io, architecture, SVG, PNG, and manifest assets are intentionally left untouched for the later publication pass. Formal publication evidence [site-a11w-paper-alignment]: normalized Draw.io and architecture sidecars plus native fixed-light SVG/PNG pairs were regenerated from the checked-in bilingual specs. Final PNG dimensions are 2285×745 (English) and 2285×745 (Chinese); SVG viewBoxes are 2283×743 and 2283×743. The final exports were inspected without clipping, node overlap, connector-node crossing, fallback text, or adaptive colors.
